cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: An index is a separate sorted structure, usually a B-tree, that lets the database find rows by a column value without scanning the whole table, turning a linear scan into a logarithmic lookup. Like a book's index.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Index columns used in WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY on hot queries; build composite indexes in the order queries filter. Every index costs storage and slows every insert and update. Denormalization and in-memory caches like Redis are the other levers for latency and throughput.

questions.a: Each index must be updated on every write, slowing inserts and updates and using disk and memory.
Those used in WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY on hot queries.
